subject: Innova Labs consumption delta & right-size proposal — upcoming term
messages:

Cc: Procurement <procurement@innovalabs.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:13:00 -0700
Subject: Usage drop and upcoming renewal — can we review?

Hey Ben,

Hope you’re well. We’re looking at our Q1 exports and noticed a ~28% drop in token consumption on the assistant endpoint vs. the prior quarter. Our renewal for the base commitment is up in mid-June and procurement asked me to pull together a short health recap so we can decide whether to renew the same commit, add burst credits, or move to a dedicated pool for latency-sensitive flows.

Quick context:
- Peak requests still look healthy but average LLM calls per user declined (we think due to a feature toggle we rolled back in March).
- We saw two SLA latency spikes on 2027-04-11 and 2027-04-23 (attached timestamps).
- We’d like an ops-oriented readout and a recommendation on cost/term tradeoffs — our finance team is open to a term extension if it reduces unit cost.

Can you and your team run a short health check and share a right-size recommendation + rough ROI for term-extension vs. burst credits? Ideally before our procurement deadline on June 10.

Thanks,
Alex Moreno
Head of Platform Integrations
Innova Labs

Attachment: innova_usage_q1.csv (CSV; 42 KB)

Alex — thanks for the note and the CSV. Putting Monica (CS/ops) and Priyom (account exec) on this thread so we can triage quickly.

Initial read:
- A 28% quarter-over-quarter drop suggests product-side usage changes more than platform throttling; good call on the feature toggle.
- We’ll validate the two latency spike windows and correlate with model variants and routing at those times.

Immediate next steps (I'll own):
1) Monica: run the token distribution + latency correlation and share a short report (ETA Wed EOD).
2) Priyom: draft 2 commercial options we can present to procurement — (A) 12-month term with modest uplift + burst credits; (B) 18-month term with 15% effective unit discount and dedicated pool for 20% of traffic.
3) I’ll prepare a one-page ROI snapshot to compare both options against current run-rate.

Alex — are you ok if we share the diagnostic and proposed commercials with your procurement contact on the CC? I assume yes but wanted to confirm.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Ben Carter

Ben / Alex — ran the diagnostics and attached a short packet. Summary below.

Attachment: innova_token_breakdown_report.pdf (PDF; 560 KB)
Attachment: redwood_rightsize_recommendation.xlsx (XLSX; 120 KB)

Executive summary:
- Root cause of consumption delta: a ~32% reduction in non-streaming prompt volume originating from the mobile client after the feature toggle. Server-side calls (webhooks, batch) are steady.
- Latency spikes on 2027-04-11 & 04-23: correlated with a temporary routing to a lower-capacity model variant during autoscaling hiccups; we recommend pinning critical flows to a dedicated variant when latency SLOs are required.
- Token distribution: 62% system + instruction tokens (stable), user prompt tokens dropped 28% QoQ.

Right-size recommendation (operations + cost):
- Option A (short): 12-month renewal, keep current base commit, add 25% burst buffer (prepaid credits). Expected unit cost: +2% vs current, flexible burst for seasonal spikes.
- Option B (efficiency + SLA): 18-month commitment, shift 20% of steady traffic to a dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) with autoscale headroom; apply 15% effective discount on CPU/GPU token rates. Upfront commitment required; runway + priority routing reduces latency incidents and predicted overage spend by ~40% over 12 months.

ROI snapshot (conservative):
- Option A: neutral to +3% savings depending on burst utilization; minimal ops lift.
- Option B: 12–18% net savings over 18 months after accounting for reserved capacity and expected growth; significantly better latency profile for critical flows.

Questions for Innova procurement:
- Do you have a target ARR budget or preferred term length?
- Would you be open to an 18-month uplift if we include a fixed SLA credit schedule for latency exceedances?

I can walk through the spreadsheet on a 30-min call. Priyom, can you draft a commercial with both options and a baseline quote?

—
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Usage drop and upcoming renewal — can we review?

Thanks for the clear analysis — this is super helpful. Procurement is inclined toward Option B (18-month with a dedicated pool for ~20% of steady traffic) provided a few items are nailed down:
- Confirmed SLA credits tied to p99 latency on dedicated pool (we’ll need specific targets and credit mechanics).
- A revised commercial (quote) including: committed token qty, price per token, upfront payment schedule, and a DocuSign-ready contract.
- Ability to shift an initial 20% of traffic to the dedicated pool within 2–3 weeks of signing.

We’re on a procurement cadence: decision targeted by June 10; contracts signed by June 17 if everything aligns. Can you get a quote + DocuSign link by EOD Friday (May 28)?

Also: we’d like to include a 90-day review milestone post-signing to validate actual savings and SLA behavior.

If that works I’d like Ben to distribute an updated quote and the contract to procurement so they can start their internal review.

Alex

Innova Labs
